summary: Every independently selectable undirected-edge indicator can change the requested degree vector, and the accepted row scan visits the quadratic adjacency-matrix input once, so its upper bound matches the problem-level lower bound.

optimality.argument: The upper triangle contains N(N-1)/2 independent edge indicators, and changing any one changes the degrees of its two endpoints; an exact algorithm must determine all of them, while summing every row performs constant work per matrix entry.

replacement_checks.evidence: If one upper-triangle edge indicator were not determined, toggling only that edge would change two required output entries without being detected, establishing Omega(N^2).
The accepted implementation sums each of the N rows once and processes each of the N^2 binary entries exactly once, establishing O(N^2) time.

The certificate regression compares both exact packaged sources with an independent upper-triangle edge oracle over every simple graph through N=6, deterministic random legal graphs, all authored cases, and maximum-size empty, complete, path, and star graphs.
